Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:10:1.hebrew: ושתים היה שוה - והלוה תובע את המלוה את יתר דמיו, וקא סבר האי תנא: המלוה על המשכון שומר שכר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:10:1.english: And it was worth two - And the borrower is claiming from the lender the excess of its value, and this Tanna holds [that] one who lends against a pledge is a paid bailee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:10:2.hebrew: פטור - הלוה מן השבועה, שאין כאן הודאה במקצת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:10:2.english: Exempt - The borrower [is exempt] from the oath, for there is no partial admission here.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:11:1.english: And the other [party] produce, etc. - And disqualify him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:12:1.english: To which - does "who swears" that is taught in it [i.e., the Mishnah] refer?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:12:2.english: If we say [it refers] to the latter clause - [Referring] to the obligation of the latter clause.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:12:3.english: Derive it, etc. - And why does [the Mishnah] need to base the reason on [the concern] lest he produce the deposit and disqualify him from testimony and from an oath?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:12:4.english: What [is meant by] "to the first clause"? - Behold, the first clause teaches [that he is] exempt.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:13:1.english: To the latter part of the first clause - [This] refers to the obligation [to take an oath] that is taught in the first clause.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:13:2.hebrew: לשתבע מלוה - שלא היתה שוה אלא שקל, ויטול שקל; דכיון דאיכא שבועה על הלוה מן התורה, אי אתה יכול לפוטרו בולא כלום, ומשום תיקון עולם שלא יפסל ישראל, שקלוה לשבועה מיניה ושדיוה אמלוה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:13:2.english: Let the lender take an oath - That it was worth only a shekel, and he shall take a shekel; for since there is an oath upon the borrower by Torah law, you cannot exempt him with nothing at all, and for the betterment of the world, so that a Jew should not become disqualified, they took the oath away from him and placed it upon the lender.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:2:1.english: And the sons said: We are not paying - [He] did not manage to pay before he died.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:3:1.english: The sons paid - And the father did not manage to say, "I am paying," before he died.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:3:2.english: Who pleased me - Many times he gave me satisfaction.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:1.hebrew: שילם לבנים - מתו הבעלים ונגנבה, ואמר השומר לבנים: "הריני משלם", או שילם — מהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:1.english: [If] he paid the sons - [Meaning:] the owner died, and [the deposit] was stolen, and the bailee said to the sons, "Behold, I am paying," or he [actually] paid [them] — what is [the law]?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:2.hebrew: או דלמא - כיון ששניהם הראשונים הוה להו נייחא נפשא בהדדי, קנו כפילא אף בנים מן הבנים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:2.english: Or perhaps - Since both of the original [parties] had mutual satisfaction with each other, even sons acquire the double payment from the sons.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:3.hebrew: שלמו בנים לבנים מהו - דליכא שום צד נייחא נפשא באלו שהם קיימים, שלא הם ולא אביהם עשו קורת רוח לאלו, ולא אביהם של אלו קיבל קורת רוח מבני השומר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:4:3.english: [If] sons paid sons, what [is the law]? - For there is no aspect of satisfaction of mind at all among those who are alive, [since] neither they [the bailee's sons] nor their father gave satisfaction to these [the owner's sons], nor did the father of these [the owner] receive satisfaction from the bailee's sons.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:1.english: [If] he paid half - From the outset he said, "I am paying half and no more."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:10.hebrew: מהו - לקנות הכפל? מי אמרינן, כיון דקרן לאו דבעל הוא, לאו תשלומין מעליא נינהו ולא קני כפילא; או דלמא, כיון דאפוטרופוס הוא על הנכסים ואוכל הפירות, בעלים הוי עלייהו ותשלומין הן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:10.english: What is [the halakha] - [With respect to] acquiring the double payment? Do we say [that] since the principal does not belong to the husband, it is not a proper payment and [the borrower] does not acquire the double payment; or perhaps, since he is an administrator over the property and consumes the produce, he is [considered] the owner over them and it is [a valid] payment?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:11.english: A woman who borrowed - For the needs of her melog land.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:2.english: What is [the law] - [Regarding] acquiring half of the double [payment]?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:3.hebrew: שאל שתי פרות - אם תימצי לומר לא קני מחצה, שאל שתי פרות ונגנבו, ואמר הריני משלם אחת, ולא אמר מתה מחמת מלאכה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:3.english: [If] one borrowed two cows - If you conclude [that] half [payment] does not acquire [the double payment], [what if] one borrowed two cows and they were stolen, and he said, "I am paying [for] one," and he did not say, "It died on account of work"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:4.hebrew: מהו - לקנות כפל שלה? מי אמרינן כיון דפרה שלימה שילם, קנה, או דלמא כיון דתרוייהו חד פקדון הוו ואינו משלם את שתיהם, לא אקני ליה כפילא, שהרי הוא נפסד על ידו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:4.english: What is [the law] - to acquire its double [payment]? Do we say [that] since he paid [for] a whole cow, he acquires [it]; or perhaps, since both of them are one deposit and he does not pay [for] both of them, [the owner] does not transfer the double [payment] to him, for behold, he suffers a loss through him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:5.hebrew: ושילם לאחד מהם - חלקו, חצי דמיה שעליו, מהו לקנות חלקו המגיעו? מי אמרינן כל הקרן שלו שילם, או דלמא בעינן עד שישלם כל הפרה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:5.english: And he paid one of them - [He paid] his share, half of its value that he owes — what is [the law] regarding acquiring his portion that comes to him? Do we say [that] he paid all of his principal, or perhaps we require [that he pay] until he pays [for] the entire cow?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:6.english: And one of them paid - half of its value that is [incumbent] upon him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:7.hebrew: מהו - שיקנה חצי הכפל? מי אמרינן, הרי שילם כל המוטל עליו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:7.english: What [is the law] - [Namely,] that he should acquire half of the double payment? Do we say: "Behold, he has paid all that is incumbent upon him"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:8.hebrew: שאל מן האשה - פרה של נכסי מלוג, שהקרן שלה והפירות לבעל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:8.english: [If] one borrowed from a woman - A cow of melog property, where the principal is hers and the produce [belongs] to the husband.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:5:9.english: And he paid - [the value of] the cow to the owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:6:1.hebrew: משביעין אותו - אמתני' קאי, אע"פ שהוא משלם, כדקתני: שילם ולא רצה לישבע, משביעין אותו שבועה שאינה ברשותו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:6:1.english: We administer an oath to him - [This] refers to the Mishnah: even though he pays, as [the Mishnah] teaches, "[If] he paid and did not wish to take an oath," we administer to him an oath that it is not in his possession.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:7:2.hebrew: פטור - הלוה מן השבועה, שאין כאן הודאה במקצת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:7:2.english: Exempt - The borrower [is exempt] from the oath, for there is no partial admission here.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:8:1.hebrew: חייב - לישבע שכך היה שוה, ומשלם לו דינר שהודה לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 34b:8:1.english: Obligated - to take an oath that it was worth that much, and he pays him the dinar that he admitted to him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:11:1.hebrew: שמא יוציא הלה הפקדון - פירש רש"י: ויפסלנו לעדות ולשבועה. וקשה לר"ת, דכל שכן שישבע הלוה, שהוא ידקדק יותר לישבע באמת כדי שלא יפסלנו המלוה; וכי עבדינן תקנה לרמאי? וכי תימא דחיישינן שמא המשכון יתקלקל אחרי כן ויוציא עליו לעז אע"פ שנשבע באמת — א"כ מאי פריך בסמוך: "כי משתבע מלוה נמי, לטרח לוה ולייתי"? והשתא אי שוה יותר, אם כן נשבע לשקר, וכל שכן שיזהר בשבועתו. ונראה לרבינו תם כפירוש רבינו חננאל, דנראה כמו שבועה לבטלה, וגנאי הוא לישבע היכא שהדבר מתברר אחרי כן שהמלוה יוציא את הפקדון; אבל כי רמינן לה על המלוה, לא ישבע עד שידע שלא יוכל למצאה. וא"ת: אמאי לא חשיב הא בפרק כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מד: ושם ד"ה ואלו) עם הנשבעין ונוטלין? דליכא למימר "תנא ושייר", ד"אלו" קתני, כדדייק בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ט': ושם) גבי "אלו מעניקין להם". ויש לומר דלא חשיב התם אלא אותם שאין יכולין לישבע: כגון גזלן וחובל — דניכרים הדברים, כיון שנכנס שלם בביתו ונתקוטטו ויצא חבול, שהוא חבלו; וכן בחנוני, אינו יכול לישבע בעה"ב שאינו יודע אם נתן חנוני לפועלים; וכן שכיר, שאין בעה"ב יכול לישבע לפי שהוא טרוד בפועליו. ומהאי טעמא נמי במוציא הוצאות על נכסי אשתו, אמרי' בפרק האשה שנפלו לה כו' (כתובות דף פ. ושם ד"ה ישבע): ישבע כמה הוציא ויטול, דאין האשה יודעת כמה הוציא בעלה, ולא חשיב לה פ' כל הנשבעים דהוי בכלל שכיר. אבל הכא, הלוה יכול לישבע דקים ליה טפי ממלוה, אך שלא רצו חכמים גזירה שמא יוציא הלה כו': [וע"ע תוס' כתובות פ. ד"ה ישבע ועוד שם פז: ד"ה ואלו]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:11:1.english: Lest the other produce the deposit - Rashi explained: and he will disqualify him from testimony and from [taking] an oath. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for all the more so should the borrower take the oath, since he will be more careful to swear truthfully so that the lender will not disqualify him; and do we make an enactment for a deceiver? And if you say that we are concerned lest the collateral deteriorate afterward and [the lender] will spread a false rumor about him even though he swore truthfully — if so, why does [the Gemara] object immediately below: "When the lender swears as well, let the borrower trouble himself and bring [it]"? Now, if it is worth more, if so he swore falsely, and all the more so he will be careful in his oath. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam like the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel, that it appears like an oath in vain, and it is unseemly to swear where the matter becomes clarified afterward when the lender produces the deposit; whereas when we place [the oath] upon the lender, he will not swear until he knows that he cannot find it. And if you ask: Why does [the Mishnah] not count this in the chapter Kol HaNishba'in (Shevuot 44b, and there s.v. Ve'eilu) among those who swear and collect? For one cannot say "[the Tanna] taught [some] and omitted [others]," since it teaches "These [are the ones]," as [the Gemara] infers in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b, and there) regarding "These are the ones to whom we grant severance gifts." And one can say that it only counts there those where [the defendant] cannot swear: such as a robber and an assailant — for the matter is evident, since [the victim] entered his house whole and they quarreled and he came out injured, that he injured him; and similarly with a shopkeeper, the employer cannot swear because he does not know whether the shopkeeper gave [goods] to the workers; and similarly a hired worker, where the employer cannot swear because he is preoccupied with his workers. And for this reason as well, regarding one who incurs expenses on his wife's property, we say in the chapter HaIshah SheNaflu Lah etc. (Ketubot 80a, and there s.v. Yishava): he swears how much he spent and collects, because the wife does not know how much her husband spent; and the chapter Kol HaNishba'in does not count it because it is included in [the category of] a hired worker. However here, the borrower is able to swear, as he knows better than the lender, except that the Sages did not want [him to], as a decree lest the other produce [the deposit] etc. [See also Tosafot on Ketubot 80a, s.v. Yishava, and further there 87b, s.v. Ve'eilu].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:1:1.hebrew: וחזר ואמר איני משלם [מאי] מי אמרינן מהדר קהדר ביה - מכאן מוכיח ר"ת, דאם אמר לחברו: "השבע וטול", קודם שנשבע יכול לחזור בו ולומר: "אשבע ולא אשלם". ובפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכח. ושם), דאמר: "עבדי גנבת", והלה אומר: "אתה מכרתו לי, רצונך השבע וטול", ונשבע אינו יכול לחזור בו — לא גרס "נשבע" בלא וא"ו, דמשמע שבע"כ ישבע. ובריש שבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף לט. ושם ד"ה אם), דאמר: "אם אמר איני נשבע פוטרין אותו מיד" — לא כפרש"י, שפוטרין אותו לפי שאינו יכול לחזור בו, אלא יש לומר: מסלקין אותו מב"ד, כדי שיתבייש לחזור ולומר "אשבע". מיהו, שוב פירש ר"ת בתשובה אחת, דשפיר גרסינן "נשבע" בלא וא"ו, וישבע בע"כ. והא דאמרינן בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כד. ושם: ד"ה שלח) גבי "נאמן עלי אבא ואביך": מחלוקת לאחר גמר דין, אבל קודם גמר דין דברי הכל יכול לחזור בו — הכא אפילו קודם שנשבע אינו יכול לחזור בו, דכיון שקבל עליו לשלם אם ישבע זה שכנגדו, הוי כמו לאחר גמר דין. והכא דקאמר "מהדר קהדר ביה", לא שיוכל לחזור, אלא רוצה הוא לחזור אף על פי שאינו יכול, ולא מקני ליה כפילא משום דאטרחיה לב"ד, כדאמר בסמוך גבי ההוא דאפקיד כיפי. וכה"ג איכא בפ' יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלח.): "מדאשתיק קננהו, וכשצוח לבסוף מהדר קהדר ביה" — פירוש: רוצה לחזור ואינו יכול:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:1:1.english: And then said: I will not pay, [what is the halakha?] Do we say he is retracting - From here Rabbeinu Tam proves that if one said to his fellow, "Swear and take [it]," before he swears he can retract and say, "I will swear and not pay." And in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 128a, and there [in Tosafot]), where [the Gemara] says: "[If one says,] 'You stole my slave,' and the other says, 'You sold him to me; if you wish, swear and take [him],' and he swore, he cannot retract" — [Rabbeinu Tam] does not read nishba ("he swears") without a vav, which would imply that he must swear against his will. And at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 39a, and there s.v. im), where it says, "If he said, 'I will not swear,' they dismiss him immediately" — [this is] not like Rashi's explanation, that they dismiss him because he cannot retract; rather, one should say [that] they remove him from the court so that he will be embarrassed to retract and say, "I will swear." However, Rabbeinu Tam subsequently explained in a responsum that we do indeed read nishba without a vav, and he must swear against his will. And [as for] that which we say in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 24a, and there 24b s.v. shalach) regarding [the case of], "My father and your father are trustworthy to me": the dispute [is only] after the verdict is finalized, whereas before the verdict is finalized everyone agrees he can retract — here, even before he swears, he cannot retract, because once he accepted upon himself to pay if the opposing party swears, it is considered like after the verdict is finalized. And here, when [the Gemara] says, "he is retracting," [it does] not [mean] that he is able to retract, rather [that] he wants to retract even though he cannot, and [the owner] does not transfer the double payment to him because he troubled the court, as [the Gemara] says nearby regarding that [man] who deposited earrings. And similarly, there is [a passage] in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 138a): "Since he was silent, he acquired them, and when he cried out at the end, he is retracting" — meaning, he wants to retract, but he cannot.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:2:1.hebrew: הריני משלם ומת כו' - תימה, היאך ישלם לבני הנפקד כפל? הא אין אדם מוריש קנס לבניו, כדתנן בריש פרק נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף מא:):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:2:1.english: "I hereby [choose to] pay," and he died, etc. - It is astonishing: how would [the thief] pay double to the sons of the bailee? Behold, a person does not bequeath a fine to his sons, as we learned in the Mishnah at the beginning of the chapter Na'arah Shenitpatah (Ketubot 41b):

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:5:1.hebrew: שאל מן האשה - פי' רש"י: פרה מנכסי מלוג, שהקרן שלה ופירות לבעל. וקשה: דמאי קבעי? דכי שאל פרה מן האשה, כאילו שאל הפירות מן הבעל, וכששילם הפרה לבעל, כאילו שילם הקרן לאשה! ויש ליישב, ששילם לבעל חלקו כמו שהיתה שוה לפירותיה ולא שילם הקרן, וגרע משילם לאחד משותפים חלקו, דהתם שילם קרן; ודוחק. ויש לפרש: שאל מן האשה כשהיתה פנויה, שהיו שלה הקרן והפירות, וניסת — דהשתא שילם הפירות לבעל, אפילו נתן הכל לאשה, דכיון דניסת יש לו פירות כדין נכסי מלוג. וכן אשה ששאלה כשהיא פנויה וניסת ושלמה, דהשתא שילם הבעל דהוו הפירות שלו. והריב"ן פי': שאל מן האשה ומתה ושילם לבעל, מהו? דאפילו אם תמצא לומר דשילם לבנים קנה כפילא משום ניחותא דאבוהון, אבל בעל לא חייש לניחותא דאשה; וללישנא דמעכשיו, אשה אינה חסה על בעלה. וכן אשה ששאלה ומתה ושילם בעל — אפי' אם מפקיד מקני כפילא לבני נפקד משום דרחים להו משום אבוהון, אבל לא מקני להו לבעל משום אשתו שמתה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 34b:5:1.english: One borrowed from a woman - Rashi explained: [he borrowed] a cow from [her] melog property, where the principal is hers and [the] produce [belongs] to the husband. And this is difficult: for what is [the Gemara] asking? For when he borrowed a cow from the woman, it is as if he borrowed the produce from the husband, and when he paid [for] the cow to the husband, it is as if he paid the principal to the woman! And it can be resolved that he paid the husband his share, according to what it was worth for its produce, and did not pay the principal; and this is worse than [the case where] he paid one of [two] partners his share, for there he paid principal; and [this resolution is] forced. Alternatively, one can explain: he borrowed from the woman while she was unmarried, when both the principal and the produce were hers, and she [subsequently] married — so now he paid the produce to the husband, even if he gave everything to the woman, for once she married he has [rights to the] produce according to the law of melog property. And similarly, a woman who borrowed [an item] while she was unmarried, and married, and paid — for now the husband paid, since the produce is his. And the Rivan explained: he borrowed from the woman, and she died, and he paid the husband — what is [the halakha]? For even if you conclude that [when] he paid the sons [of a deceased depositor], he acquires the double payment because of their father's satisfaction, a husband, however, does not care about his wife's satisfaction; and according to the version [that the owner transfers it] "from now" [me'akhshav], a woman does not have [sufficient] regard for her husband. And similarly, a woman who borrowed [an item], and she died, and [her] husband paid — even if a depositor transfers the double payment to the sons of a [deceased] bailee because he loves them on account of their father, he does not transfer [it] to the husband on account of his wife who died.
